explanation_en: This idiomatic phrase literally translates to 'remains in the air' and is used to describe a decision, plan, or issue that is left unresolved, uncertain, or pending. It is highly common in both informal conversations and news reports to indicate that nothing has been finalized yet.

examples.en_text: This weekend's trip is still up in the air because we don't know if it's going to rain.
examples.target_text: El viaje de este fin de semana todavía queda en el aire porque no sabemos si va a llover.

examples.en_text: The question about the budget remained unresolved and nobody answered it.
examples.target_text: La pregunta sobre el presupuesto quedó en el aire y nadie la respondió.

examples.en_text: With the cancellation of the event, all of our plans are left up in the air.
examples.target_text: Con la cancelación del evento, todos nuestros planes quedan en el aire.

examples.en_text: If the director resigns, the future of the project will remain up in the air.
examples.target_text: Si el director renuncia, el futuro del proyecto quedará en el aire.

examples.en_text: They said they would help us, but that promise always remains up in the air.
examples.target_text: Dijeron que nos ayudarían, pero esa promesa siempre queda en el aire.

examples.en_text: At the end of the meeting, many important proposals were left unresolved.
examples.target_text: Al final de la reunión, muchas propuestas importantes quedaron en el aire.

explanation_en: This extremely common idiomatic expression is used to introduce an additional fact that makes a situation even better, or more frequently, even worse (similar to 'to top it off' or 'on top of that'). It uses the past subjunctive of 'ser' ('fuera') in a fixed conditional structure. It is highly natural and essential for achieving native-like fluency.

examples.en_text: The flight was delayed three hours and, as if that weren't enough, they lost my suitcase.
examples.target_text: El vuelo se retrasó tres horas y, por si fuera poco, perdieron mi maleta.

examples.en_text: Today I've had a very long day at the office and, as if that weren't enough, now my car isn't working.
examples.target_text: Hoy he tenido un día larguísimo en la oficina y, por si fuera poco, ahora no me funciona el coche.

examples.en_text: The restaurant was very expensive and the food was cold; as if that weren't enough, the waiter was quite rude.
examples.target_text: El restaurante era muy caro y la comida estaba fría; por si fuera poco, el camarero fue bastante antipático.

examples.en_text: My brother has an exam tomorrow and, as if that weren't enough, he has just started to run a fever.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano tiene un examen mañana y, por si fuera poco, acaba de empezar a tener fiebre.

examples.en_text: The apartment is small, doesn't have natural light and, as if that weren't enough, the rent is extremely expensive.
examples.target_text: El piso es pequeño, no tiene luz natural y, por si fuera poco, el alquiler es carísimo.

examples.en_text: We were already late for the concert and, as if that weren't enough, it started to rain heavily.
examples.target_text: Ya íbamos tarde al concierto y, por si fuera poco, empezó a llover muchísimo.

explanation_en: This common phrase is used to introduce a widely known fact, equivalent to 'it is no secret that...' in English. While simple, it is a key transition phrase in journalism, debates, and essays to state an obvious truth without sounding overly aggressive. It is a useful stylistic tool for B2/C1 learners to structure their arguments smoothly.

examples.en_text: It is no secret that Juan likes his coworker.
examples.target_text: No es un secreto que a Juan le gusta su compañera de trabajo.

examples.en_text: It is no secret to anyone that the company is going through a financial crisis.
examples.target_text: Para nadie es un secreto que la empresa está pasando por una crisis financiera.

examples.en_text: It is no secret that my big dream has always been to travel all over the world.
examples.target_text: No es un secreto que mi gran sueño siempre ha sido viajar por todo el mundo.

examples.en_text: It is no longer a secret that traffic in this city is terrible at six in the evening.
examples.target_text: Ya no es un secreto que el tráfico en esta ciudad es terrible a las seis de la tarde.

examples.en_text: It has never been a secret that the education system needs an urgent reform.
examples.target_text: Nunca ha sido un secreto que el sistema educativo necesita una reforma urgente.

examples.en_text: It is no secret to my friends that I prefer to stay home on weekends.
examples.target_text: No es un secreto para mis amigos que prefiero quedarme en casa los fines de semana.

explanation_en: This expression literally means 'to be left in the dark,' but is commonly used in the context of power outages and blackouts. It uses the verb 'quedarse' to indicate a change of state, which is a key grammatical pattern for advanced learners. It is highly common in everyday speech when referring to electricity cuts.

examples.en_text: Suddenly, it started to rain very hard and the whole street was left in the dark.
examples.target_text: De repente, empezó a llover muy fuerte y toda la calle se quedó a oscuras.

examples.en_text: If we don't pay the electricity bill this week, we will be left in the dark.
examples.target_text: Si no pagamos la factura de la luz esta semana, nos quedaremos a oscuras.

examples.en_text: As soon as the movie started, the theater went dark and everyone fell silent.
examples.target_text: En cuanto empezó la película, la sala se quedó a oscuras y todos guardaron silencio.

examples.en_text: We were cooking dinner when the power went out and we were left in the dark.
examples.target_text: Estábamos cocinando la cena cuando se fue la luz y nos quedamos a oscuras.

examples.en_text: I don't like to be left in the dark when I'm home alone, it scares me a little.
examples.target_text: No me gusta quedarme a oscuras cuando estoy solo en casa, me da un poco de miedo.

examples.en_text: There was a problem with the office fuses and we were left in the dark in the middle of the meeting.
examples.target_text: Hubo un problema con los fusibles de la oficina y nos quedamos a oscuras a mitad de la reunión.

explanation_en: This is a very common idiomatic construction used to express 'so far this [period of time]' (e.g., 'en lo que va de año' or 'en lo que va de mes'). It is a non-obvious grammatical structure for learners because it literally translates to 'in what goes of.' It is frequently used in news, reports, and everyday conversations to track cumulative statistics.

examples.en_text: So far this year, the company has doubled its profits.
examples.target_text: En lo que va de año, la empresa ha duplicado sus ganancias.

examples.en_text: It has rained a lot so far this month.
examples.target_text: Ha llovido muchísimo en lo que va de mes.

examples.en_text: I have already read two books so far this week.
examples.target_text: Ya he leído dos libros en lo que va de semana.

examples.en_text: So far this century, technology has completely changed our lives.
examples.target_text: En lo que va de siglo, la tecnología ha cambiado nuestras vidas por completo.

examples.en_text: So far this season, our team hasn't lost a single game.
examples.target_text: En lo que va de temporada, nuestro equipo no ha perdido ningún partido.

examples.en_text: I have received more than twenty emails so far this morning.
examples.target_text: He recibido más de veinte correos en lo que va de mañana.

explanation_en: This fixed collocation means 'to put to the test' or 'to strain' a system, relationship, or ability. It is a direct equivalent of the English idiom but uses the preposition 'a' instead of 'bajo' or other options, which is a common pitfall for learners. It is highly versatile and appears frequently in both formal journalism and informal discussions.

examples.en_text: These constant problems put our patience to the test.
examples.target_text: Estos problemas constantes ponen a prueba nuestra paciencia.

examples.en_text: The boss put my skills to the test during my first day of work.
examples.target_text: El jefe puso a prueba mis habilidades durante mi primer día de trabajo.

examples.en_text: We have to put the new system to the test before launching it on the market.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que poner a prueba el nuevo sistema antes de lanzarlo al mercado.

examples.en_text: This difficult situation will put our friendship to the test.
examples.target_text: Esta difícil situación pondrá a prueba nuestra amistad.

examples.en_text: I don't want you to put my trust to the test in that way.
examples.target_text: No quiero que pongas a prueba mi confianza de esa manera.

examples.en_text: The coach is putting the players to the test in today's training.
examples.target_text: El entrenador está poniendo a prueba a los jugadores en el entrenamiento de hoy.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'entrenched' (as in military trenches), 'atrincherarse' or 'estar atrincherado' is commonly used metaphorically in political and social contexts to describe someone who refuses to change their position or compromise. It is a high-level vocabulary word (B2/C1) that adds a native, sophisticated touch to a learner's vocabulary. It is often followed by the preposition 'en' or used with adverbs like 'ideológicamente'.

examples.en_text: The suspect remained barricaded in his house for hours before surrendering.
examples.target_text: El sospechoso se quedó atrincherado en su casa durante horas antes de entregarse.

examples.en_text: Both political parties remain entrenched in their positions and there is no agreement.
examples.target_text: Los dos partidos políticos siguen atrincherados en sus posiciones y no hay acuerdo.

examples.en_text: The protesters have barricaded themselves in the university to protest against the new law.
examples.target_text: Las manifestantes se han atrincherado en la universidad para protestar contra la nueva ley.

examples.en_text: My boss is dug into her opinion and doesn't want to listen to our suggestions.
examples.target_text: Mi jefa está atrincherada en su opinión y no quiere escuchar nuestras sugerencias.

examples.en_text: The cat is holed up under the bed because the fireworks scare him.
examples.target_text: El gato está atrincherado debajo de la cama porque le asustan los fuegos artificiales.

examples.en_text: Some managers remain entrenched in the past and do not want to use new technologies.
examples.target_text: Algunos directores siguen atrincherados en el pasado y no quieren usar las nuevas tecnologías.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to go to the floor,' this idiom is used to describe a sudden, drastic drop or collapse in confidence, mood, prices, or value. While highly common in Southern Cone Spanish (Argentina, Uruguay), it is widely understood. It carries a strong visual connotation of hitting rock bottom.

examples.en_text: When it rains, my energy plummets and I don't feel like doing anything.
examples.target_text: Cuando llueve, la energía se me va al piso y no tengo ganas de hacer nada.

examples.en_text: After that lie, his reputation hit rock bottom and nobody trusts him.
examples.target_text: Después de esa mentira, la reputación se le fue al piso y nadie confía en él.

examples.en_text: If they cancel the project now, our team's motivation is going to plummet.
examples.target_text: Si cancelan el proyecto ahora, la motivación del equipo se nos va a ir al piso.

examples.en_text: Why does your mood plummet every time you talk to your boss?
examples.target_text: ¿Por qué el ánimo se te va al piso cada vez que hablas con tu jefe?

examples.en_text: In the winter season, sales plummet for swimwear stores.
examples.target_text: En la temporada de invierno, las ventas se les van al piso a las tiendas de ropa de baño.

examples.en_text: When she saw that the concert had been canceled, her excitement hit rock bottom.
examples.target_text: Cuando vio que el concierto se había cancelado, la ilusión se le fue al piso.

explanation_en: The verb 'prescindir' means to do without or dispense with something or someone, and always requires the preposition 'de'. In professional contexts, 'prescindir de alguien' is a standard, polite, and slightly formal way to say 'to lay someone off' or 'to let someone go' (literally, 'to dispense with their services').

examples.en_text: Since the company was in crisis, they laid him off without prior notice.
examples.target_text: Como la empresa estaba en crisis, prescindieron de él sin previo aviso.

examples.en_text: He was a good employee, but they did without him because the project ended.
examples.target_text: Era un buen empleado, pero prescindieron de él porque el proyecto terminó.

examples.en_text: We thought he was indispensable, but in the end they did without him and nothing changed.
examples.target_text: Pensábamos que era indispensable, pero al final prescindieron de él y nada cambió.

examples.en_text: Unfortunately, they laid him off to reduce office costs.
examples.target_text: Lamentablemente, prescindieron de él para reducir los costes de la oficina.

examples.en_text: He didn't get along with the boss, so sooner or later they let him go.
examples.target_text: No se llevaba bien con el jefe, así que tarde o temprano prescindieron de él.

examples.en_text: They hired an external agency and did without him.
examples.target_text: Contrataron a una agencia externa y prescindieron de él.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to soak' or 'to drench,' the pronominal form 'empaparse (de algo)' is used metaphorically to mean deeply absorbing information, learning a topic thoroughly, or getting fully involved in a situation. It is a very natural, expressive verb preferred by native speakers over basic verbs like 'aprender' or 'informarse'.

examples.en_text: To learn a language well, you have to immerse yourself in the local culture.
examples.target_text: Para aprender bien un idioma, tienes que empaparte de la cultura local.

examples.en_text: Before starting the new job, I soaked up all the information about the company.
examples.target_text: Antes de empezar el nuevo trabajo, me empapé de toda la información sobre la empresa.

examples.en_text: We spent the whole afternoon in the museum to immerse ourselves in the city's art.
examples.target_text: Pasamos toda la tarde en el museo para empaparnos del arte de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: I like to read historical novels to soak up the atmosphere of that era.
examples.target_text: Me gusta leer novelas históricas para empaparme de la atmósfera de esa época.

examples.en_text: We went to the mountains over the weekend to soak in the peace and quiet.
examples.target_text: Fuimos a la montaña el fin de semana para empaparnos de paz y tranquilidad.

examples.en_text: The students absorbed the professor's knowledge during the lecture.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes se empaparon de los conocimientos del profesor durante la conferencia.

explanation_en: A direct translation of the English term 'white-collar job,' this collocation is widely accepted and used in professional, economic, and sociological contexts in Spanish. It contrasts with 'trabajo de cuello azul' (blue-collar work). It is an essential term for advanced learners discussing modern labor markets.

examples.en_text: My brother prefers a white-collar job in an office to working in construction.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano prefiere un trabajo de cuello blanco en una oficina que trabajar en la construcción.

examples.en_text: With the growth of technology, there are more opportunities to get a white-collar job.
examples.target_text: Con el crecimiento de la tecnología, hay más oportunidades para conseguir un trabajo de cuello blanco.

examples.en_text: Although a white-collar job is not physically tiring, it can cause a lot of mental stress.
examples.target_text: Aunque un trabajo de cuello blanco no es físicamente cansado, puede causar mucho estrés mental.

examples.en_text: My parents worked hard so that I could have a white-collar job in the future.
examples.target_text: Mis padres trabajaron duro para que yo pudiera tener un trabajo de cuello blanco en el futuro.

examples.en_text: After years in the factory, he finally got a white-collar job and now wears a suit.
examples.target_text: Después de años en la fábrica, él finalmente consiguió un trabajo de cuello blanco y ahora usa traje.

examples.en_text: Many professionals with white-collar jobs now have the option to work from home.
examples.target_text: Muchos profesionales con trabajos de cuello blanco ahora tienen la opción de trabajar desde casa.

explanation_en: This common idiomatic construction means to have all circumstances, advantages, or luck on your side. Note the use of the preposition 'a' (literally, 'to your favor'). It is highly versatile and frequently used in sports, business, and personal advice to encourage someone.

examples.en_text: You are young, you have experience, and you speak three languages; you have everything going for you to get that job.
examples.target_text: Sos joven, tenés experiencia y hablás tres idiomas; tenés todo a tu favor para conseguir ese puesto.

examples.en_text: If you keep training like this, you have everything going for you to win next month's race.
examples.target_text: Si sigues entrenando así, tienes todo a tu favor para ganar la carrera del próximo mes.

examples.en_text: Her new company has everything going for it: a great idea, capital, and a very hard-working team.
examples.target_text: Su nueva empresa tiene todo a su favor: una gran idea, capital y un equipo muy trabajador.

examples.en_text: Students who master English have everything going for them when looking for a scholarship abroad.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes que dominan el inglés tienen todo a su favor cuando buscan una beca en el extranjero.

examples.en_text: Don't be afraid to open your own restaurant; you have everything going for you because you cook amazingly.
examples.target_text: No tengas miedo de abrir tu propio restaurante; tenés todo a tu favor porque cocinás increíble.

examples.en_text: The weather is perfect and the car is ready; we have everything going for us to make this trip a success.
examples.target_text: El clima es perfecto y el coche está listo; tenemos todo a nuestro favor para que este viaje sea un éxito.
